general_information.Description: This course introduces the fundamental principles of robotic mechanical manipulation, focusing on the mathematics and control theories that govern how robots move and interact with their environment. Students will learn spatial descriptions and transformations in 3D space, forward and inverse manipulator kinematics, velocity and force analysis using Jacobians, manipulator dynamics, and trajectory generation. The course also covers linear control strategies for achieving desired motion performance along planned trajectories. Through progressive programming assignments and MATLAB-based simulations, students gain hands-on experience applying theoretical concepts to practical manipulator problems. This foundational knowledge prepares students for advanced topics in autonomous systems, intelligent robotics, and real-world robotic application development.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time - Use laptop in class only for learning purpose - Promptly access to the FU FLM at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information
general_information.Tools: - Webots – 3D robot simulator. - CoppeliaSim - supports kinematics & dynamics. - Gazebo – well-integrated with ROS. - Python (with robotics-toolbox-python by Peter Corke). - Tool for Design and simulation of control systems. - Tool for Symbolic computation for kinematics and dynamics.

description: This course introduces the fundamental principles of robotic mechanical manipulation, focusing on the mathematics and control theories that govern how robots move and interact with their environment. Students will learn spatial descriptions and transformations in 3D space, forward and inverse manipulator kinematics, velocity and force analysis using Jacobians, manipulator dynamics, and trajectory generation. The course also covers linear control strategies for achieving desired motion performance along planned trajectories. Through progressive programming assignments and MATLAB-based simulations, students gain hands-on experience applying theoretical concepts to practical manipulator problems. learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Understand Robotics and Manipulation Fundamentals: Students can describe the basic concepts of robotic mechanical manipulation, including robot types, coordinate frames, spatial descriptions, and homogeneous transformations in 3D space.
Analyze Manipulator Kinematics: Students can apply forward and inverse kinematics methods using the Denavit–Hartenberg convention to determine the position and orientation of robotic manipulators.

Evaluate Velocity, Force, and Dynamics: Students can utilize Jacobian-based analysis to relate joint velocities and static forces, and formulate the dynamic equations of motion governing manipulator behavior.
Design and Plan Robot Trajectories: Students can generate and evaluate smooth joint-space and Cartesian-space trajectories for robotic manipulators based on motion planning principles.
Apply Linear Control Strategies: Students can design and analyze linear control schemes to achieve stable and accurate trajectory tracking performance for robotic manipulators.

Implement and Simulate Manipulator Systems: Students can develop and test manipulator software through progressive programming assignments and simulation tool, applying theoretical concepts to practical robotic problems.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Assignment 1 — Kinematics (Sessions 22–24, Week 4 ): - Select a 2–3 DOF robot and build the DH parameter table - Analyze Forward Kinematics: compute full T_0n transformation matrix - Solve Inverse Kinematics using geometric and algebraic methods - Implement in Python/MATLAB: fkine(), ikine(), plot() visualization - Scope: Chapter 1 → Chapter 4 Assignment 2 — Dynamics & Control (Sessions 52–54, Week 9 ): - Compute Jacobian matrix J(q) and identify singularity configurations - Formulate manipulator dynamics using Newton-Euler equations - Design joint-space and Cartesian-space trajectories - Build PD/PID control loop in simulation tool and analyze performance - Note: uses the same robot selected in Assignment 1 - Scope: Chapter 5 → Chapter 8
